pr_body:
Fixes #93678.

Apply remove_redundant_jumps in optimise_cfg because it belongs there. Later in move_cold_blocks_to_end, we may need to apply it again. 

Added an assertion just before assembly stage that there are no redundant jumps.

Also tidy up an unrelated error handling issue I spotted.

I'd rather fix the underlying issue.
Why does the Gentoo Non-Debug build have asserts on? That doesn't sound like non-debug to me.

Changing the `#ifdef Py_DEBUG` to `#ifndef NDEBUG` should work, but I thought `#ifdef Py_DEBUG` implied `#ifndef NDEBUG`  ande vice-versa.

Am I wrong, or the gentoo non-debug build mis-configured somehow?
`NDEBUG` can always be used independent of `Py_DEBUG`.  _(ex: we regularly build Python and the world `-UNDEBUG` mode at work in the default build that people test against)_
as for how it happened in this case, CFLAGS adds -UNDEBUG in https://github.com/python/buildmaster-config/blob/0669211daf34f86e879868364efe15683da0e069/master/custom/factories.py#L277

issue_context.title: Direct unit tests for compiler optimisations
issue_context.body:
We currently do not have a way to directly test compiler optimisations, and the tests we have are not always reliable ([more background](https://github.com/faster-cpython/ideas/issues/405)).

We need to be able to feed a sequence of bytecode instructions into the optimiser from python, and get its output back into python. Then we can write tests.
comments:
The PR seems to have increase stack consumption slightly. Some tests are now failing on WASI because the WASM runtime is running out of stack space, https://buildbot.python.org/all/#/builders/1046/builds/278

In the past I have solved similar issues by replacing a hard-coded limit (e.g. 1000) with the current recursion limit. WASI has a lower default recursion limit.

Thanks for the ping. I would guess it's because we now have things like `compiler_new_block` calling `cfg_builder_new_block`. It basically glue to avoid changing all the calls. I'll inline/replace them in a future PR.
I have added a temporary band-aid in GH-95296. Feel free to remove the skips if you have a solution for the additional stack use.
